Implementation complete. `analysis.py` (self-contained, deterministic) ran end-to-end and produced all five required artifacts. All four of your conditions are satisfied; details below.

## Results

**Stage 1 — M–R** (family R = R0·M^(−1/3)·(1−(M/Mmax)^p)^q, Mmax=1.32):
- Fit: R0 = 8468.8 km, p = 1.2996, q = 0.3752 → χ² = 6.64/11 dof, RMSE = 123.8 km, max|z| = 1.57 (no residual >2σ).
- Summary radii: R(0.6) = 8498.26, R(1.0) = 5410.08, R(1.2) = 3557.30, R(1.3) = 1776.17 km; mass_limit_solar = 1.32.
- Mmax sensitivity (condition 4, visible as orange band in the plot and in summary.json): Mmax=1.315 → R(1.3)=1644 km, R(1.32)=0.3 km; 1.325 → 1881 / 1010; 1.33 → 1967 / 1273. χ² stays 6.3–6.9 across the band, so the data cannot discriminate it.
- mr_reconstruction.csv: 24 rows, strictly decreasing (11924.4 → 0.243 km), all positive.

**Stage 2 — profiles** (Lane–Emden polytropes truncated at ρ/ρc = 1e-4 per the manifest surface threshold; n(M) = n0 + n1·M jointly fit to all 44 fragment observations):
- Fit: n0 = 1.3168, n1 = 0.7867 → χ² = 54.78/42 dof, max|z| = 2.84. n(0.6) = 1.789, n(1.0) = 2.103, n(1.3) = 2.339.
- npz is self-describing: density_fraction (3,99), enclosed_mass_fraction (3,99), mass_solar (3,) = [0.6, 1.0, 1.3], radius_fraction (99,) = i/98. Rows start at (ρ=1, m=0) and end at (ρ=1e-4, m=1).

## Your conditions
1. **Mmax traceability** — summary.json → context.mmax_assumption states explicitly that 1.32 is an inference from the holdout-grid endpoint (last mass exactly 1.320, spacing 0.095→0.001), not a measurement (data span 0.249–1.219; a free fit prefers Mmax ≥ 1.5). The plot suptitle carries the same statement.
2. **Sanity checks** (in analysis.py, printed and stored): R strictly decreasing over the 24 query masses = True; all query radii positive = True (min 0.243 km at M=1.32); for all three profile masses enclosed_mass_fraction(x=1) = 1.000000 and density_fraction(x=1) = 1.00e-04, with density monotonically decreasing and mass fraction monotonically increasing = True.
3. **The x≈0.5 "non-monotonicity" — resolved as an artifact, not a real feature.** Re-reading the fragment table, the triplet 0.251 → 0.319 → 0.221 mixed radius fractions: 0.251 is at x = 0.583, while 0.319/0.221 are at x ≈ 0.49. At matched x the observed densities are monotonic in M (x≈0.49: 0.402 → 0.319 → 0.221; x≈0.59: 0.251 → 0.088). Residual diagnostics under the joint fit: M=0.36 all |z| ≤ 1.1; M=1.16 has two ~2σ points of opposite sign (no pattern); M=0.84 has exactly one isolated −2.4σ point (x=0.49, obs 0.319 vs pred 0.244, σ=0.027) with every other point at |z| ≤ 0.9. Per-station free n* = 1.613±0.021 / 1.922±0.026 / 2.279±0.032 agree with the linear trend within ~2 station-σ (the 0.84 dip is the single high point pulling it down). Δχ² = 7.5 for 1 extra dof (per-station freedom) is marginal, and a quadratic n(M) (n2 = 0.590) achieves exactly the per-station χ² (47.27) — i.e., its "improvement" is degenerate with per-station flexibility, not evidence of a physical non-monotonic feature. Verdict: noise; the linear n(M) is retained. I quantified the consequence for the M=1.3 profile: under the quadratic alternative ρ(0.5) shifts 0.144 → 0.117 (−0.027) and m(0.5) 0.693 → 0.724 — this is the model-form uncertainty on the top-mass profile. All of this is recorded in summary.json → context.nonmonotonic_x0p5_check.
4. **Sensitivity band** rendered in panel (a) (orange fill between the Mmax=1.315/1.325/1.33 curves + legend entry), and the npz includes mass_solar and radius_fraction as agreed.

## Environment note (transparency)
matplotlib is not installed in this environment and there is no network access to install it, despite the declared runtime. analysis.py keeps the full matplotlib code path (used when available) and falls back to a built-in pure-stdlib PNG rasterizer (5×7 bitmap font, line/curve/error-bar/legend primitives) — the PNG in results/ was produced by that fallback: 1300×1050, 2×2 panels (M–R with data/band/query points/Mmax marker; density profiles; mass-fraction profiles; n(M) with station n* points), verified by decoding the PNG and checking ink coverage in all four quadrants. In a matplotlib-equipped environment the same script renders the higher-fidelity version.

## Remaining uncertainties
- R(1.32) = 0.24 km (≈0) if Mmax is exactly 1.32, up to ~1273 km if Mmax = 1.33 — the dominant uncertainty, inherited from the grid-endpoint inference.
- R(1.3) = 1776 km, range 1644–1967 across the Mmax band.
- M=1.3 profile shape: n extrapolated to 2.34 (quadratic alternative: 2.47); mid-radius density uncertainty ≈ ±0.03.
- Profile family reduced χ² ≈ 1.3 — the polytropic family is a good but not perfect match to the generator.
